Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were
involved in while riding as a passenger. Can you confirm you're comfortable continuing?
A: Yes, that's fine.
Q: Where were you seated when the collision happened?
A: I was in the front passenger seat of the car.
Q: Can you describe what the driver was doing right before impact?
A: We were turning left at an intersection in Houston, Texas. The light had just changed, and we were going through
the turn when another vehicle came from the opposite direction and hit us on the driver's side.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: Not really. It happened fast. I saw a flash of headlights and then we were hit.
Q: How fast do you think you were going?
A: We weren't going very fast, probably around the speed you'd expect for a left turn at an intersection. I'd say slow.
Q: Did you hit anything inside the vehicle, or were you thrown against anything?
A: My body jerked forward and then back into the seat. My head didn't hit anything, but my lower back took a hard jolt.
Q: Have you sought medical attention since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that same day. They said I had a back strain and gave me some medication
and told me to rest.
Q: Are you currently experiencing any symptoms?
A: Yes, my lower back is sore, especially when I sit for a long time or bend over. Some mornings it's stiff.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to get my back feeling normal again.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>
